head.citation-title: Experimental investigation and statistical evaluation of mechanical properties of centrifuged PHC pipe pile concrete
head.abstracts: © 2025 Institution of Structural Engineers. Published by Elsevier Ltd. All rights are reserved, including those for text and data mining, AI training, and similar technologies.Due to the inherent differences in molding processes, the test results obtained from traditional vibrated concrete specimens may not reliably represent the true mechanical properties of centrifuged prestressed high-strength concrete (PHC) pipe pile concrete. To address this limitation, a specialized laboratory-scale centrifuge was developed in this study to fabricate prismatic centrifuged concrete specimens. The mechanical properties of centrifuged concrete under different steam curing regimes were systematically investigated and compared with those of vibrated concrete, with particular attention to strength, stiffness, and fracture energy. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) was conducted to evaluate the effects of molding methods and steam curing regimes on all mechanical response variables, supplemented by an examination of pore structure differences. The results demonstrate that centrifuged concrete exhibits significantly improved mechanical properties compared with vibrated concrete. Extending the pre-curing time from 2 h to 4 h enhances strength development but inhibits the growth of fracture energy. Moreover, prolonged steam curing exerts a pronounced negative effect on the mechanical properties of vibrated concrete, whereas it shows a slightly positive effect on centrifuged concrete. The optimal performance of centrifuged concrete, characterized by the lowest porosity and superior mechanical properties, was achieved with a pre-curing time of 4 h and a holding time of 9 h.

Moreover, prolonged steam curing exerts a pronounced negative effect on the mechanical properties of vibrated concrete, whereas it shows a slightly positive effect on centrifuged concrete. The optimal performance of centrifuged concrete, characterized by the lowest porosity and superior mechanical properties, was achieved with a pre-curing time of 4 h and a holding time of 9 h.
